claims.text: Prolonged use of social networking sites may be related to signs and symptoms of depression.
Certain social networking site activities might be associated with low self-esteem, especially in children and adolescents.
Social networking can have a positive impact on self-esteem.
The relationship between social networking site use and mental problems remains controversial.

evidence.description: Several studies cited in the review indicated that prolonged use of SNS, such as Facebook, may be related to depression symptoms.
Some authors indicated an association between certain SNS activities and low self-esteem in children and adolescents.
Studies reviewed presented opposite results showing a positive impact of social networking on self-esteem.
Literature review reveals mixed and conflicting results regarding SNS use and mental health outcomes.

methodologies.name: Literature Review
methodologies.description: A concise narrative review of recent findings regarding social networking sites and mental health issues.

limitations.text: Research on the connection between SNS use and mental health problems faces numerous methodology challenges and yields controversial, conflicting results.
